en: The Triplet on Having the Path as Object (Maggārammaṇattika)
Dependent on a state having the Path as its object, a state not having the Path as its object arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state having the Path as its object, a state not rooted in the Path arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state having the Path as its object, a state not dominated by the Path arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a state having the Path as its object... [and so forth].
States that have a path as their object and do not have the path as their dominant influence arise by way of the root condition.
Dependent on a state that has the path as its object, states that do not have the path as their root and do not have the path as their dominant influence arise by way of the root condition.
Dependent on a state that has the path as its object, states that have neither the path as their object nor the path as their root arise.

By way of root condition. Dependent on a state that has the Path as its object, there arise states that do not have the Path as their object, do not have the Path as their root, and do not have the Path as their predominance, by way of root condition. (Abbreviated. There are thirty-five [modes] under root;
twenty-six under object ... pe ... thirty-five under non-disappearance. (To be expanded in all cases.)
